summary: Regression PASS after Skia RoundedRect -> Path.addRRect(Skia.RRectXY(...)) change in src/game/render/character.tsx. Portrait 390x844 on public preview. (1) Menu -> PLAY -> difficulty-club loads match-screen with the court AND 4 layered player figures (two near, two far, each with shoes/bottom/top/body/hair/paddle visible) — no blank canvas, no red error screen, no runtime JS errors. Initial score-display reads exactly '0 – 0 – 2' (doubles). (2) Serve hint 'Your serve — swipe up to serve' visible; a 15-step upward swipe transitions phase from waiting_serve to rally and increments Rally 0 -> 1 (dev debug overlay confirms seed+phase+fps). (3) pause-button opens pause-overlay with EXACTLY resume-button, mute-button, restart-button, quit-button; mute-button label toggles 'Sound: On' <-> 'Sound: Off' on tap; resume-button closes the overlay (count = 0) and returns to play. (4) Dev 1v1: dev-singles-button loads a match whose score-display shows EXACTLY two numbers ('0 – 0'), serveLabel ends with '· Singles', 2 player figures render (one near, one far), and a serve-swipe increments Rally 0 -> 1. Verified character layered renderer uses Skia.Path.Make().addRRect(Skia.RRectXY(...)) for 'bottom' (line 97-99) and 'top' (line 101-106) with corner radius bounded strictly < half the shorter side (r = min(bodyW,h)*0.49) — matches the proven pattern that native Skia accepts. No new deprecation warnings or regressions introduced; carryover deprecation warnings (SkPath.*, props.pointerEvents, shadow*) unchanged from iteration_3. Backend testing skipped per request (client-only app, no backend).

action_items: No regression — Skia RoundedRect replacement is working on web. Original crash is native-only (Expo Go/CanvasKit-strict) and cannot be reproduced on the web preview per the context note; a device/native smoke on Expo Go is recommended before closing.

Optional carryover: migrate all Skia.Path.Make() + addRRect/moveTo/etc. in character.tsx/CourtRenderer.tsx/GameCanvas.tsx to Skia.PathBuilder.Make() to clear deprecation noise and future-proof against upcoming removal.
critical_code_review_comments: character.tsx 'bottom' (lines 96-100) uses Skia.Path.Make().addRRect(Skia.RRectXY(rect, bodyW*0.3, bodyW*0.3)). With bodyW=1.05*scale and height=bodyH*0.42≈1.09*scale, corner radius 0.315*scale is well below half the shorter side (~0.525*scale) — safe for strict native Skia validation.

character.tsx 'top' (lines 101-107) explicitly clamps r = min(bodyW,h)*0.49 (strictly < half) before passing to RRectXY — this is exactly the invariant native Skia enforces, so the regression fix is defensively correct.
No <RoundedRect> JSX remains in character.tsx; the previously-crashing path is fully replaced. Other render files (CourtRenderer.tsx, GameCanvas.tsx) already used the Path+addRRect pattern.
match.tsx:212 (CourtRenderer) sits inside a single GestureDetector/Pan — the one-gesture-one-shot invariant from iteration_3 is preserved; the render change did not touch input.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 4 regression flows pass on web preview)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Portrait 390x844. Public URL: https://pickle-arcade.preview.emergentagent.com. Allow ~10s on /match for CanvasKit WASM. Serve-swipe recipe: mouse.move(195,650) -> down -> 15 steps up to y≈300 with ~12ms waits -> up. Verify players rendered by screenshot (expect 4 figures for CLUB doubles, 2 for dev singles). To reproduce the original native crash you MUST use Expo Go on a real device — the web preview (CanvasKit) is lenient and will NOT surface the 'Invalid properties for rounded rect' error. Expo Router keeps the previous route mounted after replace(), so if asserting a single testID across navigations use .first.
rca_of_issue: Native Skia validates RRectXY corner radii: radius must be strictly less than half the shorter side of the enclosing rect, and <RoundedRect> native binding is stricter than the web CanvasKit build. The fix replaces the JSX <RoundedRect> component with the imperative Skia.Path.Make().addRRect(Skia.RRectXY(rect, rx, ry)) pattern, with the 'top' case explicitly clamping r = min(bodyW,h)*0.49 (strictly < half). Regression check on web confirms the renderer still draws all character layers for both doubles (4 figures) and dev singles (2 figures). A device smoke on Expo Go remains advisable to confirm the native-only crash is gone, but the code pattern now matches other render files that are known to work natively.
